findings.finding: At the Barclays conference on 2026-09-10, eleven weeks into Q3, CEO Jim Koch said the summer 'did not improve' from Boston Beer's point of view and that the trend 'has not been good'. The last numbers were 29-week depletions at -5%, Q2 at -6%, and a CFO statement in July that current trends point to the low end of the FY volume guide (down low to mid single digits). A third weak quarter puts full-year depletions at or below the low end, which makes a cut or narrowing of the volume guide and a softer 2027 setup likely. Revenue consensus of -2.6% leans on shipments, not depletions.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-04-30: the volume guide was narrowed down (from flat-to-down-mid to down low-to-mid) together with a $216m litigation charge, and the stock fell 9.59%. 2026-07-23: the volume guide was unchanged with a 'low end' warning, but the GM floor was raised and marketing spend cut, and the stock rose 3.23%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, but the stock rallied from 172.55 (09-11) to about 191 since, and the average target sits around $194-205, so the market is not positioned for a guide cut. If it were priced, the stock would have stayed near its late-September low and previews would model a reduced volume guide. UBS (10-16) says only that the 'achievability' of the FY outlook is the focus.
findings.independence: Category data points the same way but is a proxy (see the category finding: Constellation beer depletions -0.6% for June-August, retail bev-alc -0.9% over the 12 weeks to 09-27 with beer a larger drag). RBC on 2026-10-20 expects soft volumes (https://www.marketscreener.com/news/boston-beer-s-stock-underperformance-unlikely-to-change-on-q3-results-rbc-says-ce785cd8da8bf625).

findings.finding: Arithmetic from the company's own documents: marketing spend (advertising, promotion and selling) rose $2.5m in Q1 and $26.2m in Q2, so $28.7m in H1. The FY guide was cut on 07-23 to $0-20m. H2 spend must therefore fall $8.7-28.7m YoY, about $0.60-2.00 per share after tax at a 29-30% tax rate on about 10.3m shares. Q3 is the larger-volume half of H2, so this is cost support for a beat against EPS consensus of $4.21-4.30 (Q3 2025: $4.25), even on weak volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: EPS $4.25 against $3.34 (+27%), stock +5.45%. Q2 2026: EPS $3.65 against $4.83 (-24%) on a $26.2m spend step-up, stock still +3.23% on the spend cut and GM raise. The stock has reacted to the cost and guide story more than to the EPS line.
findings.why_not_priced: EPS consensus is flat YoY at $4.21-4.30 and has been 'stable over the past 30 days' (Zacks). If analysts had phased an H2 spend decline of up to $29m into Q3, Q3 EPS would sit above last year's $4.25 by more than a cent or two. Last quarter's consensus missed the spend phasing by $1.18.
findings.independence: The Q1 spend figure comes from a different document (Q1 call, 2026-04-30, https://vectorshift.ai/research/companies/boston-beer-co/earnings/2026-q1). Koch said on 2026-09-10 that about $20m of lower-return spend was pulled back (same Barclays transcript as the volume finding). The CFO also said on the Q2 call that H2 spend would still be up YoY, which is inconsistent with the guide arithmetic, so the phasing is uncertain.

findings.finding: The Q3 shipments guide (down low to mid single digits, 07-23) runs against a very easy comparison: Q3 2025 shipments were -13.7% and revenue -11.2% to $537.5m. Consensus revenue of $523m (-2.6%) implies shipments of about -4% after 1-2% price. That is inside the company's guide, so the reported revenue line should land near the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue was in line ($568.3m against $566.7m) and the stock rose 3.23%. StockStory says SAM has missed revenue estimates several times over the past two years.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: consensus sits inside the guide. The small positive is the supply-chain shift (distributor inventory held at 4-4.5 weeks), which takes Q3 shipments timing off the depletion trend.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 comparison: https://www.streetinsider.com/Press+Releases/Boston+Beer+Reports+Third+Quarter+Financial+Results/25495199.html. Same company document as the marketing-spend finding.

findings.finding: This is the first print under an interim CFO. Diego Reynoso resigned on 2026-08-17 (leaving 09-30). Matthew Murphy, the Chief Accounting Officer, has been interim Treasurer and CFO since 09-15 while a formal search runs, with a retention bonus of up to $700k. A finance chief in transition, setting the first 2027 colour, raises the odds of a conservative guide or a narrowing toward the low end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Murphy was interim CFO from March to September 2023. No guidance-change reaction can be separated cleanly from that period in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a quiet 8-K that no preview except UBS's 'other news' mentions. If it were priced, previews would discuss guide-reset risk; they discuss volume only.

findings.finding: The short is crowded and has been covering into the print. About 1.59m shares were short at 09-30 (15.4% of shares outstanding, more of the Class A float), 5.1 days to cover, roughly flat since mid-September. The stock has risen from 162.49 (09-29) to about 191 intraday on 10-22, including +5% today on volume running below average, with no news found. Any print that is not clearly bad meets a squeeze mechanism; a bad one meets a run-up that has raised the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Five of the last seven prints were up. Q2 2026 rose 3.23% despite a 24% EPS miss, with short interest about 15% at the time (07-15 settlement: 1.57m shares).
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price. What is not visible is how much of the 1.59m has already covered in the 18% rally; the 10-15 settlement is not published until 10-26.
findings.independence: Daily tape from Yahoo chart v8 (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/SAM?range=2mo&interval=1d), read 2026-10-22.

findings.finding: An 8-K dated 2026-08-10 discloses a Rule 10b5-1 plan to repurchase up to $25m of Class A stock between 2026-09-28 and 2026-12-25 (about 1.3% of a $1.9bn market cap), on top of $54.1m bought year to date through 07-17. About $174m remains under the authorisation, and the company holds $265.5m of cash with no debt.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buybacks have run every quarter; no reaction can be attributed to them alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and public. A Q3 repurchase figure or a new authorisation in the release would be the only new element.
findings.independence: The Q2 release confirms the cash and the remaining authorisation (https://sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/949870/000119312526314187/sam-ex99.htm).

findings.finding: Category proxies for SAM's Q3 (06-28 to about 09-26) are soft. Constellation Brands, which reported in early October after SAM last spoke, had beer depletions of -0.6% and shipments of +5.5% (channel fill) for June-August; the stock fell on beer volumes. A trade-press summary of retail scanner data put US bev-alc dollar sales at -0.9% for the 12 weeks to 2026-09-27, with beer a larger drag and RTDs no longer offsetting. Hard seltzer and FMB were already in decline in spring data (FMB dollars -4% for the 52 weeks to 2026-04-19).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history. SAM's own depletions have lagged the category by several points every quarter in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: weak category trends are in the wire ('already_in_the_wire' in the sweep). It is filed small as a proxy.
findings.independence: Proxy, not company-confirmed. Second series: https://www.vinetur.com/en/amp/20261006108443/us-retail-alcohol-sales-fell-09-in-the-third-quarter.html (2026-10-06, snippet only; the fetch returned 429). It points the same way as the Koch finding, but these are separate sources.
